# T5b exact oracle (Z3, LinDistFlow)

Encoding in `src/p3/oracle_exact.py`: envelope bounds, LinDistFlow voltages (v = vm^2), benign limits, rule; line apparent power through a 16-gon relaxation that over-approximates both the benign set and the firing set, so UNSAT is a sound certificate for the linear model. One query per topology (16 topologies). SAT means at least one topology is SAT.

| rule | result | topologies SAT | topologies UNSAT | total solve time s | max per query s |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| R1 | SAT | 16/16 | 0/16 | 2.423 | 0.109 |
| R2 | SAT | 2/16 | 14/16 | 14.851 | 1.738 |
| R3 | UNSAT | 0/16 | 16/16 | 1.262 | 0.002 |

See `lindistflow_error.md` for the LinDistFlow error table (G6).

## R3 in the exact layer

R3 is syntactically expressible (all its measurements are linear: transformer P, load P, DER P). But LinDistFlow is lossless: the transformer power equals the sum of downstream net load exactly, so the R3 residual d is identically 0 in the linear model and R3 can never fire there. Its UNSAT is therefore vacuous: it certifies nothing about R3 on the real grid, where d equals the network losses. R3 cannot be meaningfully certified in this exact layer. A loss-aware layer (for example a convex relaxation or bounds on losses) would be needed.
